gemini.name: search
gemini.description: Search upstream tools. Two modes: (1) Plain keywords -> a ranked list of matching tools with compact param signatures (name!: required). (2) To see one tool's full inputSchema, pass EXACTLY "select:<name>" where <name> is a tool name copied from a search result (e.g. "select:github__issue_write"). Do NOT put task descriptions or phrases after "select:" — only an exact tool name works; for anything else use plain keyword search. Prefix a service name (e.g. "vercel ...") to focus on that service. Each result carries "callName": pass that exact identifier to codemode (the "name" field may contain hyphens — do not copy it literally into codemode["..."]). Connected services: fake, other.

query.description: Keywords describing the capability you need

gemini.name: execute_read
gemini.description: Write JavaScript to call READ-ONLY upstream tools (get/list/search/query) via codemode.<tool>(args). This tool is annotated read-only so the client may prompt less; it runs the same sandbox as execute(). Only your return value enters the conversation. Available read-only helpers: safeAll(tasks), unwrapBatch(x), unwrap(x), readFileRange(), waitForPrChecks(), github_actions_*. Example: async () => { const r = await codemode.github__search_repositories({query:"x"}); return r.total_count; } Results differ by service: Notion/Linear mostly return objects, GitHub often JSON text or arrays, Vercel mostly objects — guard with Array.isArray(x) / typeof x === "string" before reading fields; safeAll(tasks) keeps a batch alive when one sub-task fails; grepSnippet(text, keyword, window) extracts context slices from long results (each clipped snippet is now marked truncated); codemode.unwrap(x) normalizes JSON text, {result}, {text,resources} and content arrays; fileResult(x)/prResult(x) flatten common file/PR shapes. Intl is unavailable in the sandbox: use codemode.formatDate(value, {date:true,time:true,ms:true}) or Date UTC getters. NO SILENT CHARACTER TRUNCATION: never write `l.slice(0, 150)`, `line.substring(0, N)` or any other manual per-line character cut — that silently destroys data and is the P0 bug this guidance fixes. To control context, read with codemode.readFileRange({path,startLine,endLine,maxCharsPerLine?}) (returns {lines,truncated,truncation?,nextStart,totalLines}; NO maxCharsPerLine means full lines, with it every cut line is flagged) or codemode.sliceLines(text,start,end) (line-based, reports truncated) and REPORT the truncated flag in your answer; follow nextStart to page through. grepSnippet also reports truncated on clipped windows. Never patch or write a read whose truncated flag is true — re-read the full file first. Edit with codemode.replaceLines/applyPatch; call diffSummary before writing. codemode.normalizeFile/normalizePr/normalizeIssue/normalizeResult give canonical field sets (raw kept; truncated is true on any upstream/marker/nested flag); codemode.applyFilePatch previews/writes via GitHub tools (dryRun by default; refuses truncated reads); codemode.ensureBranch/upsertPr/fetchAllPages/repoGrep wrap injected GitHub tools. Batch 11 atomic writes: when github__push_files is available, codemode.writeFiles commits all staged files in ONE push (atomic:true); if a push fails nothing is written. Without it, per-file writes are non-atomic — a mid-batch failure returns partial:true plus written[] and a compensation hint, and explicitly requesting atomic:true without push_files fails with zero writes. Unified writes: codemode.applyFilePatch/writeFiles accept {patches:[{path,patch,sha?}]} (or single path+patch), auto-fill sha from the read, precheck JSON/JS-TS before writing, and return top-level {sha,commitSha,number?,url?}; codemode.canonicalize/normalizeMerge give {number,url,sha}; codemode.createBranchIfMissing creates from base when absent; codemode.precheckText is a lightweight write-before check (JSON strict, JS/TS brackets only — not a compiler). Use codemode.services() for a cold-start snapshot of locally known services (name/toolCount/status/verifiedAt/note); it reads local state only and makes no network call. status is point-in-time evidence ("observed" = mounted with no recorded failure, "offline" = connection failed at cold start), NOT a live health check — credentials can expire at any moment and the legacy `online` flag only means "mounted at cold start". If a tool call returns invalid_token/unauthorized, the upstream needs re-auth; treat that service as stale until it is reconnected. Tool calls return Promises (await / .then / .catch work); codemode.search, listTools, remainingCalls and services are synchronous helpers. GitHub Actions read-only helpers (gateway-side REST, not upstream tools): codemode.github_actions_list_workflow_runs({owner,repo,workflow_id?,status?,branch?,per_page?}), codemode.github_actions_list_workflow_jobs({owner,repo,run_id}), codemode.github_actions_get_job_logs({owner,repo,job_id}). Each returns {ok,status,data|text,truncated} or {ok:false,status,error}; log text may be truncated — check the flag. Requires GITHUB_TOKEN. GitHub high-frequency args: github__pull_request_read is an aggregated tool — pass method:"get" | "get_files" | "get_check_runs" (pick directly, no probing round). github__get_file_contents selects a commit/ref with `ref`; `branch` is accepted as a compatibility alias (mapped to ref when ref is absent). Linear list_issues is verbose by default: pass a small `limit` (e.g. 10–20) plus a minimal `fields` array like ["id","title","status","url"], add "description" only for the issues you need, and page with `cursor`; a default 10-issue page can exceed the ~26.8KB execute output cap and be truncated.File reads: fileResult(x).content / normalizeFile(x).content / readFileRange().lines are ALWAYS the pure file body — no "successfully downloaded ..." prefix; SHA and the notice live in sha/notice metadata fields. Never strip anything yourself. Batch contract: codemode.safeAll(tasks) and codemode.unwrapBatch(x) both return a FLAT array of {ok,value} slots (success: ok:true,value; failure: ok:false,value=error text). unwrapBatch accepts a single result, an envelope, or an array and always returns the same flat shape; never hand-unwrap one more layer. Truncation: if a result carries truncated:true or a truncation object, report it and re-read with readFileRange / grepSnippet; model-facing execute results may carry a `truncation` object naming the field, totalChars/totalLines, tailTruncated and continuation hints — the tail field names are preserved. Multi-file writes: prefer codemode.writeFiles (github__push_files) for N files — it commits all files in ONE atomic push; do not loop create_or_update_file. If atomic is unavailable and you still write per-file, the result carries partial:true, written[], remaining[] and a compensation string: surface it to the user and restore the written files before retrying. CI polling: codemode.waitForPrChecks({owner,repo,pullNumber,timeoutMs?,maxPolls?}) waits up to 30s in ONE call and returns the latest {status,conclusion,checkRuns[],polls,truncated} snapshot instead of 3–4 manual polls.GitHub Issue creation: codemode.createIssue({owner,repo,title,body?,listArgs?,createArgs?,maxPolls?}) dedupes by repo+title/body, short-polls after create for the list-index delay, and returns {ok,created,reused,issue:{number,id,url,state,title}} — number is ALWAYS URL/field-derived, never an internal id; a repeated call is idempotent. Batch unwrapping: codemode.unwrapBatch(x) ALWAYS returns a flat [{ok,value}] array for a single result, {ok,value}, JSON string or nested array; codemode.unwrap(x) flattens one upstream envelope. Issue/PR results: codemode.unwrap fills a MISSING top-level number from a GitHub /issues/<n> or /pull/<n> URL (never overrides an existing number, never uses an internal id). Never hand-peel an extra {ok,value} layer. CI: codemode.waitForPrChecks({owner,repo,pullNumber,...}) waits up to 30s in one call; codemode.rerunFailedJobs({owner,repo,runId}) calls an injected upstream rerun tool and returns code UNSUPPORTED_UPSTREAM_TOOL when none is mounted (never a fake success). Branch cleanup: codemode.mergePrWithOptionalBranchDelete({owner,repo,pullNumber,head,deleteBranch:true}) deletes the source branch ONLY with the explicit flag and an injected delete tool; no default deletion. Multi-file delete/rename: codemode.deleteFiles({paths}) and codemode.renameFiles({renames:[{from,to}]}) are TWO-PHASE because push_files supports only {path,content}; results carry atomic:false and partial:true. Only an injected git-data callback can make them atomic — do not claim otherwise. writeFiles contract: call codemode.writeFiles({owner,repo,branch,patches:[{path,patch}],dryRun:false}) — `patches` with unified diffs, NOT the push_files {files:[...]}/{content} shape (it is rejected with an actionable error). Without dryRun:false nothing is committed: the result says dryRun:true, written:0 and carries a warning — never report that as a write. Merged PRs: a github__merge_pull_request result only carries {sha,merged,message}. Call codemode.normalizeMerge(result, {owner,repo,pullNumber}) (or a bare pull number) and the returned number/url are filled from that call identity — never from an internal id. Connected services: fake, other. Boundary: if the task exceeds the available tools' capabilities, requires an external service, or information is insufficient, explicitly state it cannot be done and explain why — do not force tool calls; refuse harmful requests.
